frameworks.name: Scale Zero Framework
frameworks.definition: The prerequisite stage before location replication in which the founder removes themselves entirely from operations while maintaining or improving business performance.

frameworks.name: Expansion Readiness Criteria
frameworks.definition: Two necessary conditions for opening a new location: excess profit beyond current needs and discretionary time available beyond current operations.

claims.text: Most business owners opening a second location do so from a scarcity mindset—'I'm not making enough, so I'll add another'—rather than from abundance. This backfires: the founder spreads their sweat-equity across two young locations, the original drops 20% in revenue (while costs are sunk), and total profit falls even as overhead doubles.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Founder personal effort and momentum compound on the original location over years; a new location is brand-new with no word-of-mouth, newer staff, and zero momentum. Splitting founder attention proportionally splits the growth engine.
bounded_by: Does not apply to systematized businesses where replication is automated and founder-independent

claims.text: The correct expansion trigger is when a business generates more profit than the founder can deploy and the founder has more discretionary time than they can fill—abundance on both capital and time, not scarcity on revenue.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Service or local businesses where replication involves founder bottleneck
claims.mechanism: Expansion from abundance ensures the first location is cash-flowing sustainably before capital diverts; founder's excess time capacity means they can mentor and build systems for the second location without cannibalizing the first.

claims.text: Before opening a second location, a business must achieve 'Scale Zero'—the founder removes themselves entirely from operations while the business maintains or improves performance. If the founder's absence breaks the business, the business is not ready to replicate.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Service businesses, membership businesses, local brick-and-mortar
claims.mechanism: A founder-dependent business cannot be replicated at the second location because the second location would inherit the same bottleneck. Scale Zero proves the model is systematized and can run without the founder, making replication possible.

claims.text: A founder working in the business (not delegating delivery and sales) can scale a single location to maturity, but expanding to a second location without first removing the founder from day-to-day operations creates a compounding problem: two young locations each needing the founder's personal effort.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Businesses where founder is the primary delivery mechanism (coaching, personal services, high-touch sales)
claims.mechanism: A founder's personal sweat-equity compounds value in the location where it is deployed; dividing the founder's effort across two locations divides the compounding effect, resulting in slower growth at each.
bounded_by: Does not apply to systematized businesses with documented processes and hired delivery staff

examples.text: A typical expansion story: a business owner has built one location over several years to a healthy revenue level. Eager to grow, they open a second location. Because they are the primary operator (sales, delivery, culture-setting), they must split time and attention. The original location's revenue drops 20% immediately (founder attention loss), while the new location grows slowly (no brand equity, no word-of-mouth, new untrained staff). Fixed costs for both locations are now sunk. The owner is working twice as hard as before, managing two separate teams, inventory, and client relationships, but making significantly less total profit than before.

A systematized business, by contrast, has documented its operations and hired managers to run each location independently. When this business owner decides to expand from a position of excess cash and time, they can open a second location with a strong ops manager (hired or promoted) running it under the systems already documented at the first location. The original location is unaffected; the owner coaches the new ops manager but does not personally run the location.

practices.text: Before expanding, achieve Scale Zero: operate the business without your direct involvement and confirm that revenue, margins, and team performance remain stable or improve.
Expand only when you have excess profit that you cannot redeploy into the current business and excess personal time that you cannot fill—never expand from revenue hunger or growth ambition alone.
Document every operational process (sales, delivery, team management, culture) before opening a second location, so the new location can be run by hired managers without founder involvement.
